ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The upper part of the figure is an organic fragment, with one O⁻, one OR², one CN, one R, and one R¹ substituent, and two C=C and one C≡N are drawn; the lower/right side also has a cyclic sulfur component composed of 8 sulfur atoms. The curved arrows in the figure indicate electron movement, and this problem requires ignoring these arrows. Reasoning: First count the non-hydrogen heavy-atom bonds of the upper organic fragment: C–O⁻, C–O, O–R², upper C=C, C–C between two carbon centers, C–CN, C≡N, C–R, lower C=C, C–R¹, for a total of 10. Then count the cyclic sulfur component: 8 sulfur atoms form an S8 ring, so there are 8 S–S bonds. The total is 10 + 8 = 18.

method.method_draft: First count the upper organic fragment: C–O−, C–O, O–R², the upper C=C, C–C between the two carbon centers, C–CN, C≡N, C–R, the lower C=C, and C–R¹, giving 10 heavy-atom bonds. Then count the cyclic sulfur component: the eight sulfur atoms form an S8 ring with 8 S–S bonds. Disregard the curved arrows. Add 10 + 8 to obtain 18.
